Direction B of 3 - proposal

Qalam قلم

The documentary direction. Navy is pinned at the deepest step and used the way ink is used: for the bar, for rules, for headings. Surfaces are paper with white sheets laid on them, corners are near-square, cards are separated by hairlines rather than shadows, and Arabic headings are set in Naskh while the Latin display is a serif. Status is carried by a coloured rule and the word itself, never by a flood of colour.

  • primary-950 #0B3C5D brand navy - pinned at the deepest step, action colour and ink
  • neutral-50 #FAF7F1 brand cream - table head, row hover, paper stock
  • neutral-900 #312822 warm near-black - body text, derived from the cream, not a grey
  • neutral-600 #797067 warm secondary ink - labels and metadata

Who it suits

Accounting and audit-heavy floors, distributors who print quotes, statements and delivery notes, and any client who wants the CRM to read like a ledger rather than a web app.

What it costs

Naskh is beautiful but it is not a grid typeface, so this direction needs two Arabic families (Naskh for headings, a sans for the grid) - a real maintenance and subsetting cost. Serif Latin display can read as dated to a buyer who expected SaaS.

Typefaces

Arabic: Noto Sans Arabic (grid) + Noto Naskh Arabic (headings)
Latin: Noto Sans (UI) + Noto Serif (display)
Figures: none - figures use tabular numerals

Shape

Radii control 2 (md) - card 4 (xl) - badge 2 (a squared label, not a pill)
None. Separators are 1px rules at the border tokens; nothing floats. The only depth cue is paper-on-paper.
Density rows 46px / 34px

Primary scale - derived from #0B3C5D

Eleven steps generated in OKLCH at the navy's own hue (243.9 deg) with one chroma curve, then gamut-mapped into sRGB. #0B3C5D is pinned at primary-950 because that is the step whose lightness it actually occupies - it is not moved to the middle of the scale to look tidy. Same token names in all three directions, different values.

Neutral scale - derived from #FAF7F1

Cream is pinned at neutral-50, which is where its lightness lands (0.977 against Tailwind's 0.985 for gray-50). It is not a stock Tailwind grey: the hue starts at the cream's own 84.6 deg and the ramp is built from there. White is a separate --surface-card token, not a scale step.

Radii and two density levels

Density changes padding first and type size second. In all three directions the Arabic body never drops below 16 px, so the compact level pays for its extra rows out of padding and rules, not out of legibility.

--radius-sm0px

--radius-md2px

--radius-lg3px

--radius-xl4px

--radius-pill2px

Fonts, licensing and self-hosting

The product is installed per client and must not reach a CDN for anything, so every face below is embedded in this file as base64 TTF and is shipped inside the installation. Formats are unsubsetted here (the honest cost of a no-network sheet); a production build would ship WOFF2 subsets.

FamilyLicenceDeliverySource of the licence claim
Noto Sans ArabicSIL OFL 1.1self-hostedfonts-noto-core (copyright file records OFL-1.1)
Noto Naskh ArabicSIL OFL 1.1self-hostedfonts-noto-core (copyright file records OFL-1.1)
Noto SansSIL OFL 1.1self-hostedfonts-noto-core (copyright file records OFL-1.1)
Noto SerifSIL OFL 1.1self-hostedfonts-noto-core (copyright file records OFL-1.1)

Every family named in this sheet is SIL OFL 1.1. That licence allows embedding, redistribution and commercial use, requires the copyright notice and licence text to travel with the font files, and forbids selling the font itself. IBM Plex carries a Reserved Font Name clause: distribute the files unmodified and under their own names.

Proposal, not a decision. This sheet exists so the direction is chosen by looking at it. Nothing here is wired into the product; no file under packages/ was touched. Path: docs/design/specimens/qalam.html

Rendered with locally embedded fonts only - no network request is made by this page. Full rationale, contrast numbers and licensing: docs/design/rebrand-palette-directions.md
